litigation.note: Two material long-running disputes. (1) ITC Limited and its subsidiary Russell Credit Limited, members holding then 8.72% (at present 8.10%) of equity, filed a petition under Sections 241/242/244 before the NCLT in April 2019 alleging oppression and mismanagement in relation to the Company's transaction with BSREP III India Ballet Pte. Ltd. and affiliates ('Brookfield') for the sale of the Company's hotel undertakings; NCLT Mumbai allowed ITC/Russell Credit's waiver application on January 24, 2024, and the Company together with promoters Mr. Vivek Nair and Mr. Dinesh Nair has appealed to the NCLAT, Delhi, where the matter is being heard. Parallel SEBI complaints by ITC and LIC (LIC later withdrew) resulted in a SEBI order dated July 23, 2019 in favour of the Company; ITC's appeal was dismissed by SAT on September 26, 2019, and ITC's further appeal is pending before the Supreme Court of India. (2) Disputes with Airports Authority of India over lease rental and royalty (Minimum Guaranteed Amount) on the hotel land of 18,000 sq. meters and adjacent land of 11,000 sq. meters, including AAI eviction proceedings; the Bombay High Court by judgment dated June 09, 2025 directed the lease-rental dispute back to the AAI Eviction Officer and referred FSI utilisation, land amalgamation and damages to arbitration before retired Justice Mr. S.V. Gangapurwala, with both proceedings currently running. The disputes were also referred to AAI's Settlement Advisory Committee since 2020; the Company received an AAI offer letter dated December 01, 2023 for renewal of the 18,000 sq. meter lease, which it has accepted, and has sought renewal for a further period of 30 years. Amounts are deliberately not reproduced. Separately, the Directors' Report records that while there are no audit qualifications or adverse remarks, there ARE audit observations on the financial statements, explained in Notes 37.1 and 37.3.

risks.note: The hotel business continues to be dependent on domestic and global economic conditions, airline connectivity, consumer confidence and the overall geopolitical environment; ongoing geopolitical tensions in conflict-affected regions, trade disruptions, energy-price and crude-oil volatility, airfare volatility, changing travel corridors and inflationary pressure on discretionary spending may influence travel flows, operating costs and discretionary spending. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A text.)

FY 2025-26 occupancy fell to 69% from 73.80% in FY 2024-25, with revenue growth carried by ARR (Rs. 12,469 vs Rs. 11,170) and RevPAR (Rs. 8,602 vs Rs. 8,242); management describes revenue growth as achieved 'despite lower overall room inventory utilisation', and notes that protecting occupancy, average room rates and revenue quality requires sustained sales agility in an environment of geopolitical uncertainty, changing travel behaviour and higher guest expectations. (Back-filled from the strategy_outlook bundle's MD&A Business Review.)

The MD&A cites elevated cyber and security concerns in the global operating environment, and the Board-approved Risk Management Policy framework expressly covers financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability, information and cyber security risks, with measures for risk mitigation including systems and processes for internal control of identified risks and a business continuity plan.

The Directors' Report states that although there are no audit qualifications or adverse remarks, there ARE audit observations on the financial statements, with the explanation given in Notes 37.1 and 37.3 — a standing accounting/disclosure watch-item.
